name: Honda B18C5 (Acura Integra Type R, US, 1997-2001), with cam timing taken from Honda's data for the JDM B18C 96 spec.R (Integra Type R, 1995)
summary: High-revving 1.8 L DOHC VTEC inline-four that switches from mild low-speed cam lobes to a long-duration, high-lift lobe at about 5700 rpm, giving an abrupt change in intake and exhaust note, and then runs on to an 8400 rpm redline through a single-runner intake and a 4-2-1 header.

layout.note: Transverse inline-four, DOHC, belt-driven cams (belt drive per https://www.honda.co.jp/sportscar/vtec_history/B18C/).

bore_mm.note: Honda Japan press information, same bore and stroke for B18C and B18C 96 spec.R.

rod_length_mm.note: Wikipedia B18C5 entry (rod/stroke 1.58); the figure carries no citation there. Not found in a Honda document.

compression_ratio.note: US B18C5 per Honda's 2001 press release. The JDM B18C 96 spec.R is 11.1 (https://www.honda.co.jp/factbook/auto/INTEGRA/19950824/in95-005.html).

firing_order.note: Third-party spec aggregator covering the 1994-2001 Integra 1.8 L engines generally, not a Honda document. The page does not state the cylinder numbering convention (which end is No. 1); that is unconfirmed. Single bank.

intake_valve_dia_mm.note: 33 mm x 2, same diameter as base B18C; Type R valve has a thinner stem and 0.5 mm less margin thickness.

intake_lift_mm_high.note: Valve lift on the high-speed (VTEC) cam, JDM B18C 96 spec.R. Honda's US release says the US Type R high cam has 0.9 mm more intake lift than the GS-R, consistent with base B18C 10.6 mm -> 11.5 mm.

exhaust_lift_mm_high.note: High-speed cam, JDM B18C 96 spec.R. US release says +1.1 mm over GS-R, consistent with base B18C 9.4 mm -> 10.5 mm.

ivo_btdc_high.note: High cam, measured at 1 mm lift. Base B18C high cam: 10 deg BTDC.

ivc_abdc_high.note: High cam, at 1 mm lift. Base B18C high cam: 40 deg ABDC.

evo_bbdc_high.note: High cam, at 1 mm lift. Base B18C high cam: 40 deg BBDC.

evc_atdc_high.note: High cam, at 1 mm lift. Base B18C high cam: 7 deg ATDC.

intake_duration_deg_high.note: Researcher's sum of Honda's events at 1 mm lift (15 + 180 + 45). A forum cam list gives the same 240 deg at 1 mm for the Type R through 1999 and 243 deg for the 2000/01 spec (https://www.forum.civic-eg.com/viewtopic.php?f=9&t=2583, forum post, unverified).

exhaust_duration_deg_high.note: Researcher's sum of Honda's events at 1 mm lift (45 + 180 + 10). Same forum list gives 235 deg.

cam_switch_rpm.note: Low-lift to high-lift changeover on the US Type R (GS-R: 4400 rpm). Wikipedia lists 5800 rpm (96 spec) and 6000 rpm (98 spec) for the JDM engine.

redline_rpm.note: Honda's stated maximum permissible engine speed for the JDM B18C 96 spec.R. Wikipedia gives the same 8400 rpm redline for the B18C5, with fuel cut at 9000 rpm (uncited).

idle_rpm.note: 750 +/- 50 rpm on a third-party aggregator page for 1994-2001 Integra 1.8 L engines generally; not confirmed for the Type R specifically.

peak_power_kw.note: 195 hp (SAE net) converted by the researcher. JDM 96 spec.R: 200 PS at 8000 rpm.

peak_power_rpm.note: Wikipedia's B18C5 entry says 7800 rpm; Honda's own release is used here.

peak_torque_nm.note: 130 lb-ft converted by the researcher. JDM 96 spec.R: 18.5 kgm at 7500 rpm.

peak_torque_rpm.note: Wikipedia's B18C5 entry says 7500 rpm; Honda's own release is used here.

intake_type.value: plenum, single throttle body, single-port (one runner per cylinder) cast aluminium manifold
intake_type.note: The GS-R's dual-runner variable manifold is replaced by short, direct single runners.

runner_dia_mm.note: Intake runners enlarged from 35 mm (GS-R) to 42 mm.

throttle_dia_mm.note: Also 62 mm in Honda Japan's factbook (base B18C: 60 mm). Air intake duct 70 mm (base 65 mm) per the factbook.

header_type.value: 4-2-1 (Honda calls it a large-diameter Tri-Y header with a tapered collector), stainless steel

exhaust_pipe_dia_mm.note: JDM 96 spec.R exhaust pipe diameter (base B18C: 48.6-50.8 mm). Tail pipe 76 mm (base 50.8 mm).

exhaust_notes.value: All-stainless system, sharper merge angle at the collector, larger pipes, a third chamber and a high-flow silencer; Honda's US release claims 30 percent more exhaust flow than the GS-R.

missing: low-speed (non-VTEC) cam profile: lift, duration and timing for the primary and secondary lobes; not published in any Honda page found, and forum threads say the same
cam timing confirmed for the US B18C5 specifically (JDM 96 spec.R figures used; a forum list says the 2000/01 intake cam is 243 deg at 1 mm rather than 240)
rod_length_mm from a Honda source (Wikipedia value is uncited)
firing order with numbering convention from a Honda source
primary_dia_mm and primary_length_mm of the header
crank layout (flat-plane inline-four assumed by convention but not stated on any page opened)
idle_rpm for the Type R specifically

sources.what: Honda Japan press information (factbook) for the August 1995 Integra Type R: comparison table of B18C vs B18C 96 spec.R with high-cam valve timing at 1 mm lift, valve lift, valve, throttle and exhaust diameters. Manufacturer document.
Same Honda factbook: maximum permissible rpm, power and torque of the 96 spec.R.
Same Honda factbook: intake, exhaust and valve gear changes.
Honda Japan VTEC history page for the B18C 96 spec.R: basic specification table.
American Honda press release, 2001 Acura Integra Type R powertrain: compression, power, torque, VTEC changeover rpm, throttle and runner diameters, exhaust description. Manufacturer document.
Wikipedia B-series article: rod length, redline and variant list. Used only where Honda pages were silent; several entries are uncited.
Forum post listing B-series cam durations at 1 mm lift; used only as a cross-check on the durations computed from Honda's figures.
Third-party spec aggregator for 1994-2001 Integra 1.8 L engines: firing order and idle speed. Low credibility; used because no better page was found.

vehicle.name: Acura Integra Type R (DC2, US, 1997)

curb_kg.note: 'Curb Weight 2577 lbs (1170 kg)'. 1998 model year; standard not stated. Car and Driver, March 1997 (https://web.archive.org/web/20150710092135/http://www.caranddriver.com/reviews/1997-acura-integra-type-r-archived-test-review): 'Curb weight: 2560 lb'. The 2001 sheet (https://acuranews.com/en-US/releases/release-038578562975f17ab17410004c34c8a5-2001-acura-integra-type-r-specifications) gives 2639 lb (1197 kg).

gears.note: 'Ratios (:1) 1st 3.230 2nd 2.105 3rd 1.458 4th 1.107 5th 0.848 Reverse 3.000'. The 2001 sheet gives the same ratios.

wheel_radius_m.note: Calculated by me from the tyre size 195/55 R15 84V (rim diameter / 2 + section width x aspect ratio): unloaded geometric radius, not a published rolling radius.

tyre.note: 'Tires Bridgestone RE010 195/55 R15 84V' on '6.0 JJ x 15' wheels.

top_speed_kmh.note: Car and Driver test data: 'Top speed (drag limited): 143 mph'. Converted by me (230.1 km/h). A measured figure, not a maker's claim.

driven.note: English Wikipedia, 'Honda Integra' (read 2026-11-17), infobox layout: Front-engine, front-wheel drive (all-wheel drive on the Japanese DB9 only).

missing: a Honda specification sheet dated for the 1997 model year with a Type R column

sources.what: American Honda press release '1998 Acura Integra Type R Specifications', 23 April 1997: maker's specification table for the US Type R with the B18C5.
Car and Driver road test of the 1997 Acura Integra Type R (Barry Winfield, March 1997), archived copy: test weight and drag-limited top speed.
Acura '2001 Acura Integra Type R Specifications', 3 January 2001: same ratios and tyres, heavier curb weight. Cross-check.
